name: USGS San Pedro Shelf original seafloor-character, 2004 video and MLLW bathymetry

rights.license: U.S. federal public-domain source data; attribution and original metadata retained

spatial.vertical_datum: MLLW on separate OF 2004-1221 bathymetry grids only

temporal.update_cadence: historical static publication; monthly byte and availability check

evidence.supports: USGS Data Series 552 publication, methods, survey period and study area.
Original inner/outer character rasters and video-observation shapefile.
4 m categorical inner-shelf character map; code 1 means rugose rock and code 3 means mixed rock and sand.
Historical camera descriptions and source metadata; correlated observations are not fish counts.
Original San Pedro 4 m bathymetry metadata says soundings were corrected to MLLW and warns of survey artifacts.

provenance.access_service: USGS Data Series 552 original ZIP archives
transformations: Original categorical pixels opened and counted in their native UTM grid.
Original 2004 camera records sampled at native character pixels.
Connected 4 m rugose-rock components of at least 2,500 square meters with an actual hard-bottom camera observation placed in an unpublished review queue.
Three original 4 m USGS MLLW bathymetry grids sampled at every rugose-rock class cell in the review components; source-grid overlap differences recorded.

limitations: This is a historical habitat source, not a bathymetric depth surface or a current fish-abundance survey.
Twenty-four review-queue components are not fishing targets or exportable waypoints. Video records on a camera tow are correlated.

All 11,732 rock-class cells across 24 components have original 25–200 ft MLLW depth samples, but the source lacks per-cell uncertainty and has documented artifacts. A dated 2026-09-25 CDFW MPA/NOAA federal 100 m screen held none; a bounded NOAA ENC danger screen held two; all 24 lie shoreward of NOAA's official 50-fathom coordinate line. Current seasonal rules, hazards and route/access still require trip-date review.
The outer-shelf class scheme must be read from metadata, not inferred from its color palette.
